text:
Mina: quick follow-up to the staged-evict RFC — thinking about a lighter handshake that lets allocators opt into a grace window before hard demote. want to align on tradeoffs before i write the PR
Tom: sounds useful. are you proposing an explicit "grace_token" in the allocator ABI?
Mina: yes, something like that but with three phases: soft-grace (no migration), cooperative-drain (best-effort offload), and hard-demote (force spill). allocators would advertise which phases they support
Priya: curious how this interacts with KV cache reuse. if cooperative-drain is best-effort, we could end up thrashing between caches and offload path. any thoughts on metrics to gate transitions?
Mina: good point. thinking telemetry hooks: "drain_attempts", "drain_success_rate", and a bounded retry counter per allocation. if success_rate drops below threshold -> shorten grace window
Ava: also need to consider fragmentation. if we delay demotion too long we hurt compaction opportunities. maybe expose a fragmentation_score hint so evictor can pick targets that give most compaction benefit
Tom: fragmentation score + estimated reclaimable_bytes would be neat. allocator exposes both as part of its residency descriptor
Jason: operational note: Dedicated > Hosted differences. Hosted needs stricter SLOs for latency, so default grace windows shorter. private deployments can be more permissive
evict-bot: reminder: existing evictor will fallback to LRU when no coop support detected :thumbsup:
Priya: API nit: prefer feature-flagged rollout. start with opt-in header in requests: `X-Evict-Mode: coop-v2` so we can A/B and roll back quickly
Mina: agreed. rollout plan: (1) implement ABI with optional grace phases, (2) add telemetry + gating thresholds, (3) enable header rollout + perf A/B, (4) bake compaction hint integration
Ava: edge-case: what about pinned tensors with external references (PY caller holds CUDA ptr)? cooperative-drain can't move those. we need explicit failure code so caller can escalate to application-level fallback
Tom: we should return a small set of stable error codes: COOP_WOULD_BLOCK, COOP_DEMOTE_REQUIRED, UNMOVABLE_PIN. keeps SDK logic simple
Jason: can we implement a debug endpoint that returns allocator residency snapshots? would help triage regenerative thrash in early rollout
Mina: yes, add `GET /debug/allocators/<pool>/residency?sample=true` for internal use only
Priya: last concern: billing/accounting. staged demote might increase host memory usage temporarily. ops needs a flag to cap aggregate soft-grace capacity per tenant
Mina: noted — will add tenant_soft_budget param to the evictor policy config and default to a conservative value in hosted
Ava: thanks, this feels like a good next step. short PR with ABI + one-off telemetry is fine, then iter sessions for compaction hints
Tom: I'll pair on the ABI surface this afternoon
Mina: thanks all — i'll draft the PR and drop the link here when ready
Mina: (later) PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/XXXX — feedback welcome
